easy.explanation: Elihu directly addresses Job and asks him to hear his words.
easy.q: Whom does Elihu ask to hear his speeches?

easy.explanation: Elihu says, "Behold, now I have opened my mouth."
easy.q: What does Elihu say he has opened?

answers: As a man formed out of clay
easy.explanation: Elihu says, "I also am formed out of the clay."
easy.q: How does Elihu describe himself in relation to Job?

answers: Because he is also made of clay and will not be heavy upon Job
Because he does not intend to speak
medium.explanation: Elihu presents himself as a fellow human being whose terror and hand will not make Job afraid.
medium.q: Why does Elihu say Job should not be afraid of him?

answers: Answer him and stand before him
medium.explanation: Elihu says, "If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up."
medium.q: What does Elihu invite Job to do?

answers: Words of uprightness and clearly spoken knowledge
medium.explanation: He says the words of his mouth will be from the uprightness of his heart and will utter knowledge clearly.
medium.q: What does Elihu say his words will be like?

answers: There should be direct conversation and an opportunity to answer
No answer should ever be given
challenge.explanation: Elihu asks Job to listen but also invites him to answer.
challenge.q: What principle of conversation does Elihu present?

answers: He says that God created him as a human being like Job
He says that he is stronger than Job
He says that he is an angel
challenge.explanation: Elihu says that the Spirit of God made him and that he also was formed out of clay.
challenge.q: How does Elihu support his claim that he can speak with Job as an equal?

answers: He presents his words as sincere and honest
He admits that he knows nothing
challenge.explanation: Elihu claims that his words come from an upright heart and will communicate knowledge clearly.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Elihu's statement that his words are from the uprightness of his heart?

answers: That he is clean and without transgression
That he does not want to speak
easy.explanation: Elihu repeats Job's claim, "I am clean without transgression, I am innocent."
easy.q: What claim of Job does Elihu summarize?

easy.explanation: Job says that God counts him for his enemy.
easy.q: According to Elihu's summary, how does Job feel that God treats him?

answers: There is no difference between man and God
easy.explanation: Elihu says, "God is greater than man."
easy.q: What is Elihu's general response to Job's claims?

answers: Job claims innocence, and Elihu emphasizes God's superiority
Job is silent, and Elihu stops speaking
Job praises God, and Elihu denies it
medium.explanation: Elihu summarizes Job's claim of innocence and answers by stressing that God is greater than man.
medium.q: What connection does Elihu make between Job's claims and his own response?

answers: Because God does not give account of all His matters to man
Because Job has already answered Him
medium.explanation: Elihu asks why Job strives against God, since God does not give account of all His matters.
medium.q: Why, according to Elihu, is there no point in striving against God?

answers: Job believes God finds reasons to oppose him
Job believes God gives him songs
Job believes God sends him dreams
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Job's complaint that God finds occasions against him and counts him as an enemy.
medium.q: What does the phrase "he findeth occasions against me" mean in context?

answers: Man knows everything and God knows nothing
God is greater than man, so man is limited in understanding His ways
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: Elihu bases his answer on the fact that God is greater than humanity.
challenge.q: What central difference between God and man does Elihu emphasize?

answers: It highlights man's limitation in demanding a full explanation from God
It claims that God does not exist
It means Elihu withdraws his argument
challenge.explanation: Elihu uses the statement to answer Job's complaint and emphasize God's higher authority.
challenge.q: What significance is there in Elihu's statement that God does not give account of His matters?

answers: Job's claims followed by an answer about God's greatness
Illness followed by healing and confession
A dream followed by a parable and silence
challenge.explanation: Elihu first summarizes Job's words and then responds by declaring that God is greater than man.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Ways God Communicates with People

answers: Through dreams and visions of the night
easy.explanation: Elihu mentions a dream and a vision of the night.
easy.q: By what means does God speak to people in this passage?

easy.explanation: They occur when deep sleep falls upon people in slumberings upon the bed.
easy.q: When do the dream and night vision occur?

answers: To withdraw them from their purpose and hide pride from them
easy.explanation: The passage says that God opens their ears and seals instruction so that He may turn them from their purpose and hide pride from them.
easy.q: Why does God open the ears of men?

answers: God warns a person, turns him from a harmful purpose, and keeps him from destruction
A person sins, is punished, and then God remains silent
A person wakes, travels, and then dreams
medium.explanation: The dream or vision serves as a warning intended to protect the person from destruction.
medium.q: What order of events is described in the passage?

answers: The dream warns the person and keeps him from destruction
The dream prevents the person from hearing
The dream causes the person to become proud
medium.explanation: God's communication is presented as a means of correction and deliverance.
medium.q: What is the connection between the dream and the person's preservation?

medium.explanation: In this context, the pit represents destruction or death from which God preserves the person.
medium.q: What does the word "pit" suggest in the phrase "He keepeth back his soul from the pit"?

answers: God can communicate with people in more than one way
God speaks only once in a person's lifetime
God does not speak to people
challenge.explanation: The following verses describe different ways God speaks, including dreams and night visions.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement, "For God speaketh once, yea twice"?

answers: To turn a person from his purpose and hide pride from him
To give him authority over others
challenge.explanation: The purpose of the instruction is correction and preservation.
challenge.q: What is the moral purpose of the message received in a dream?

answers: Moral correction is connected with rescue from destruction
challenge.explanation: God's warning changes a person's course and helps preserve his life from destruction.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between being turned from one's purpose and being kept from the pit?

paragraphs.title: Suffering, Illness, and the Possibility of Recovery

easy.explanation: The verse says that he is chastened with pain upon his bed.
easy.q: Where is the person described as being chastened with pain?

answers: He abhors bread and dainty meat
easy.explanation: The passage says that his life abhors bread and his soul dainty meat.
easy.q: What happens to the sick person's appetite?

easy.explanation: The passage describes a messenger and a ransom as means of deliverance from the pit.
easy.q: What may lead a person from the pit to life?

answers: As pain that weakens the body and brings a person near destruction
As a blessing that increases appetite
As a dream that has no bodily effect
medium.explanation: The person suffers pain, loses his appetite, and draws near to the grave and destruction.
medium.q: How is illness described at the beginning of the passage?

answers: To show a person's uprightness and seek his deliverance
medium.explanation: The messenger is described as one among a thousand who shows man his uprightness and asks for his release from the pit.
medium.q: What is the role of the messenger or interpreter?

medium.explanation: The ransom is presented as the means by which the person may be delivered from going down to the pit.
medium.q: What does the word "ransom" mean in this passage?

answers: His flesh becomes fresh, he returns to youth, prays to God, and sees His face with joy
He turns away from God and becomes more ill
He stops speaking and remains in the pit
challenge.explanation: Deliverance brings renewal, prayer, God's favor, joy, and the light of life.
challenge.q: What change is described after the person is delivered?

challenge.explanation: The person says, "I have sinned, and perverted that which was right."
challenge.q: What does confession add to the process of deliverance?

answers: God repeatedly works with people to bring them back from destruction
People are never given another opportunity
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that God often uses these means to restore a person's soul from the pit.
challenge.q: What does the phrase "all these things worketh God oftentimes with man" emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Request to Listen and the Offer of Wisdom

easy.explanation: Elihu says, "Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me."
easy.q: What does Elihu ask Job to do at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: Elihu says, "If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak."
easy.q: What does Elihu allow Job to do?

easy.explanation: Elihu says, "I shall teach thee wisdom."
easy.q: What will Elihu teach Job if Job does not answer?

answers: Listen quietly, and answer if he has something to say
medium.explanation: Elihu asks Job to hold his peace while leaving him the opportunity to answer.
medium.q: What order of behavior does Elihu suggest to Job?

answers: If Job has nothing to say, he should listen
If Job rises from his bed
medium.explanation: Elihu says, "If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom."
medium.q: What condition does Elihu give before offering to teach wisdom?

medium.explanation: Elihu asks Job to remain silent while he speaks and teaches.
medium.q: What does "hold thy peace" mean in this context?

answers: He asks Job to be quiet for instruction but allows him to answer
He forbids Job to speak under every circumstance
challenge.explanation: Elihu leads the conversation while still inviting Job to speak if he has an answer.
challenge.q: How does Elihu combine authority with an opportunity for dialogue?

answers: He wants Job to present his case and defend himself
He has no interest in Job's response
challenge.explanation: Elihu invites Job to speak because he desires Job to set forth his justification.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Elihu's statement, "I desire to justify thee"?

answers: The passage moves from allowing Job to answer to offering to teach him wisdom
It moves from healing to describing a dream
It moves from confession to complete silence
challenge.explanation: Elihu gives Job the opportunity to respond, but if Job does not, Elihu offers to teach him wisdom.
challenge.q: What conceptual transition occurs at the end of the chapter?
